correctness.rationale: For the given bilinear table e_i e_j=e_{2j-i}, the unscaled Fourier transform of u² at t is X_{-t}X_{2t}; p is invertible and the zero frequency must vanish. The inverse transform gives descent exactly when X_{qt}=X_t^q. Every nonzero index has orbit length d, so an orbit has one freely chosen F_{q^d} coordinate, with q^d−1 nonzero choices. The condition couples cosets by multiplication by −2; its quotient cycles all have length ℓ. Loops force zero, a 2-cycle permits at most one chosen vertex, and the usual circular gap count gives the displayed coefficients for longer cycles. The binary case reduces to the order of −1 modulo the subgroup, which is one precisely when d is even. This establishes the full quantifiers without assuming associativity or using a finite experiment as a proof.
